expectations.text: Revokes ALL access including the OAuth grants/API tokens specifically (not just SSO/passwords) — and cites the integration-token risk pattern (e.g., the August 2025 Salesloft Drift breach where stolen OAuth tokens exposed Salesforce data at hundreds of organisations)
expectations.evidence: Revokes OAuth connected app tokens and API keys specifically, but cites no integration-token breach precedent (no Salesloft Drift or equivalent incident pattern) — only a generic note that "a live OAuth grant is an ongoing access risk"

expectations.text: Handles data: inventory, return in agreed format, certified deletion including backup-cycle expiry, and sub-processor deletion flow-down
expectations.evidence: "Identify all data the vendor holds"; final export for record-keeping; "written certification of deletion"; "ask how long the vendor retains data in backups"; "vendor's subprocessors... require deletion confirmation covers those as well"

expectations.text: Cleans technical debris: webhooks, connected-app registrations, service accounts, DNS/integrations
expectations.evidence: "Disable any webhooks"; "Revoke the OAuth connected app authorization"; "Disable/delete any dedicated integration user or service account"; removes IP allowlists, named credentials, remote site settings, browser extensions

expectations.text: Covers contractual closure: termination assistance obligations, records retention, surviving clauses, final settlement
expectations.evidence: Covers final invoice, survival clauses and retaining records, but omits termination-assistance obligations owed by the vendor (migration planning discussed only as internal cutover)

expectations.text: Adds post-exit verification (e.g., ~30-day log review confirming no residual access) and feeds lessons back into the vendor register/tiering
expectations.evidence: "Spot-check Salesforce logs (login history, API usage) a few weeks after revocation to confirm no residual access"; "Update your vendor risk register/TPRM system... with a closure date"
